bib.title: Leave No Context Behind: Efficient Infinite Context Transformers with Infini-attention

question: Can a Transformer LLM process arbitrarily long inputs with bounded memory and compute by adding a compressive memory to attention?
hypothesis: Reusing old KV states in a fixed-size associative compressive memory, mixed with local attention, lets models extrapolate to far longer contexts than seen in training.
contributions: Infini-attention: long-term compressive memory plus local causal attention in one block
Minimal change to standard scaled dot-product attention; supports plug-and-play continual pre-training and long-context adaptation
Streaming processing of infinitely long inputs with bounded memory and compute

method.summary: Each attention layer splits input into segments (N=2048); local causal dot-product attention per segment plus an associative-matrix compressive memory (linear attention, ELU+1, optional delta rule) holding all earlier KV; outputs mixed by a learned per-head sigmoid gate. Trained with BPTT and gradient checkpointing. Evaluated on LM from scratch, 1B passkey and 8B BookSum after continual pre-training.
method.task: long-context language modeling, passkey retrieval, book summarization

other.best_config: 100 summary vectors trained on 8196-length sequences (runs with 50/100/150 vectors, lengths 4096/8196/32768)

training.objective: inferred: next-token language modeling for LM and continual pre-training; task fine-tuning for passkey and BookSum (loss not stated)
training.lr: 0.01 for LM (searched 0.003, 0.005, 0.01, 0.03); 0.0001 for LLM continual pre-training and task fine-tuning
training.steps: 1B: 30K continual pre-training steps then 400 passkey fine-tune steps; 8B: 30K continual pre-training steps; BookSum fine-tune steps not stated
training.seq_len: LM 32768 (100K variant); 1B pretrain 4K, passkey FT 5K; 8B pretrain 8K, BookSum FT 32K
training.regularisation: gradient checkpointing after each segment (memory saving, not regularisation)

other.bptt: gradient w.r.t. compressive memory states through segments
other.position_embeddings: none on Q/K for memory read and update; applied after
other.gate: one learned scalar beta per head; sigmoid(beta)

inference.retrieval: memory retrieval A_mem = sigma(Q) M / (sigma(Q) z), not external retrieval

limits: Passkey is a synthetic needle task with one 4-digit key; says little about reasoning over long context.
Zero-shot passkey accuracy is near 0 except at the end position (97-100%), i.e. memory is not usable without fine-tuning.
Fine-tuned Linear model degrades at 1M (96/94/100) and 512K (97/99/100).
Compression is lossy by design; no analysis of what the fixed memory forgets as length grows.
Base 1B/8B LLMs unnamed; no compute, hardware, seeds, data sizes or code release; BookSum Overall metric undefined.
Baseline comparison on BookSum uses numbers copied from Bertsch et al. 2024, so setups may differ.
Memory-size comparison to Memorizing Transformers (114x) compares parameters, not quality at equal budget on all tasks.

code.snippet: A_mem = σ(Q)M_{s-1} / (σ(Q)z_{s-1}); M_s ← M_{s-1} + σ(K)^T V; z_s ← z_{s-1} + Σ_t σ(K_t); A = sigmoid(β) ⊙ A_mem + (1 − sigmoid(β)) ⊙ A_dot
